title: Chromosomes 13, 14, and 15
clinical_history: Demonstration metaphase prepared for laboratory teaching. The task is to separate the group D chromosomes. No clinical abnormality is provided.
unknown_prompt: Chromosomes 13, 14, and 15 are medium acrocentric chromosomes. Use the long-arm band order to pair them, then write the karyotype.

learning_rounds.title: 13, 14, and 15
learning_rounds.note: Chromosomes 13, 14, and 15 are medium acrocentrics. Use the long-arm band order to tell them apart. The short arms and satellites are not a reliable way to number them.

plain_language_interpretation: A normal male diploid karyotype. Chromosomes 13, 14, and 15 are each present as a normal pair.
diagnosis: No cytogenetic abnormality identified (normal male karyotype)
explanation: Group D contains three pairs of medium acrocentric chromosomes. The long-arm band pattern distinguishes 13, 14, and 15. This demonstration cell has 46 chromosomes, one X, and one Y, with no extra, missing, or rearranged chromosome.
hints: All three pairs are acrocentric. The centromere position does not choose the number.
Read the q-arm bands from the centromere toward the end of the arm.
A normal male study is written 46,XY when no further change is present.

references.label: ISCN
references.citation: McGowan-Jordan J, Hastings RJ, Moore S, eds. ISCN 2020: An International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature. Basel: Karger; 2020.
